$comment: HAND-MAINTAINED. The fal.ai endpoint roster: which endpoints unmodel serves, and under which verb.
fal's own `category` is LOSSY and is never the source of this map — music hides in `text-to-audio`,
tts is split across two categories, and edits / upscale / background-removal are all folded into
`image-to-image`. So the verb is curated here by hand and `scripts/codegen-fal.ts` reads it; the
snapshot's category is carried into data/fal/manifest.json for the audit command to diff against.
`endpoints` — one entry per curated endpoint id (the id IS the queue URL path):
verb                 REQUIRED. One of image | imageEdit | video | lipsync | upscale | avatar | threeD | tts | stt | music.
`threeD` is the one verb that is not its category's id: the category is "3d", which is
not a TypeScript identifier and so cannot be an export name or a generated file stem.
unified             set to false when the provider-native request is curated but the canonical vocabulary
cannot represent it. The endpoint stays in every direct fal artifact; only the generated
`*-params` table and its unified adapter model list omit it.
textParam            the property that carries the prompt/text, when the endpoint takes one.
allowsModelProperty  `model` is a REAL wire field on this endpoint, not a route selector.
Codegen HARD-ERRORS on a top-level `model` property unless this says true (risk R6):
unmodel routes with the `endpoint` pseudo-param, so a genuine `model` field must be
a deliberate, reviewed exception rather than a silently swallowed collision.
note                 why this id is here, or what is unusual about it.
retiredOn            ISO date fal retired it. The row still ships as status:"deprecated" (a warning, not a
compile break) until 90 days old; after that codegen hard-fails so the row cannot rot.
Every id in here must resolve against the Platform API (GET https://api.fal.ai/v1/models?endpoint_id=…);
`bun run codegen:fal:refresh` fails loudly on one that does not. Verified live 2026-08-25.
Wave 1a seeded 12 ids spanning all nine verbs. Wave 1b widened image to 28 and imageEdit to 17. Wave 1c
widened video to 30 and built out the two audio-driven categories — lipsync (8) and avatar (8) — which
are new unmodel categories, not just new fal rows. Wave 1d completed the remaining four: upscale (10 —
the third and last new unmodel category), tts (23), stt (6) and music (10). Wave 1e added the stretch
roster — four image rows and two lipsync rows — bringing image to 32 and lipsync to 10. All nine verbs
are now at their full wave-1 roster: 146 endpoints.
The v0.3.x adopter wave added SIX more, on demand rather than on a sweep, bringing the roster to 171:
five video rows (fal-ai/veo3.1/reference-to-video, fal-ai/kling-video/v3/pro/motion-control,
fal-ai/kling-video/o1/video-to-video/edit, fal-ai/minimax/hailuo-2.3/pro/text-to-video, fal-ai/lightx/relight)
and one upscale row (topaz/upscale/video/generative) — video 30 → 35, upscale 10 → 11. Two of them are
recorded exceptions to the cheapness bar rather than examples of it: the o1 edit is the PREVIOUS generation
of a line whose o3 half is already curated, and hailuo-2.3 is a generation older than the curated h3 pair.
Both were asked for by name by an adopter running them in production, and demand is a reason a roster may
act on as long as it is written down — which is what their `note` fields do.
The direct-substrate wave then added bria/fibo-edit/relight as endpoint 172. Its prompt-less request is exact
and useful through `fal.imageEdit`, while `unified: false` keeps it out of the prompt-required image-edit pack.
BACKLOG, recorded so the next widening starts from a decision: the kling o3 family. o1 has 8 video routes
and o3 has 10 (4k/{i2v,ref,t2v}, pro/{i2v,ref,t2v,v2v-reference}, standard/{i2v,ref,t2v,v2v-edit,v2v-reference}),
all active, all uncurated except the one o3 edit; curating o1's edit while ten NEWER o3 routes stay out is
arbitrary, and the honest fix is a deliberate o3-family sweep rather than more backfilling one id at a time.
Three roster facts the plan expected differently, all settled against the live listing on 2026-08-25:
fal serves NINE Kokoro languages rather than twelve (there is no German, Korean or Vietnamese endpoint);
the tts roster the plan enumerates by name comes to 23 ids rather than the 19 its heading counted; and
the two heygen v3 lipsync routes the plan lists as avatar stretch require `video_url`, so the input rule
below files them under lipsync. The stretch bar was CHEAPNESS: a row joins only if it resolves live, its
price is transcribable, and it lowers into an EXISTING shape class with no new generator work. That is
why `fal-ai/fast-sdxl` is in `excluded.endpoints` rather than here.
`upscale` is the one verb with no fixed output modality: an upscaler returns an image from
fal-ai/aura-sr and a clip from fal-ai/seedvr/upscale/video, so the modality is read off each
endpoint's own response schema. It is also why the category narrows `source` per model.
The lipsync/avatar split is by INPUT, not by vendor: an endpoint that takes a video clip is lipsync and
one that takes a still is avatar, which is why fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v3 and fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v3/image-to-video
— one product, two routes — are filed under different verbs. Two avatar rows (veed/avatars, argil/avatars)
take NEITHER: their performer is a catalogued id, which is why the category narrows `image` per model.
`threeD` splits the same way and inside one category: fal files both `text-to-3d` and `image-to-3d` here,
and each row's `inputs` says which mood that route reads. One endpoint (fal-ai/hyper3d/rodin/v2.5) reads
BOTH and requires neither. fal's 3d family also holds `3d-to-3d` — mesh in, mesh out — which is excluded
wholesale below: `unmodel/3d` asks for an object to be made, not refined.
A note on ids: several are VENDOR-namespaced (`ideogram/v4`, `openai/gpt-image-2`, `krea/v2/...`),
and for those fal's OpenAPI document is written against a different internal route — `ideogram/v4`
documents `/fal-ai/ideogram-v4`, `xai/grok-imagine-image` documents `/fal-ai/xai`. BOTH are live
(probed unauthenticated 2026-08-24: each answers 401, a fabricated id answers 404). The id here is
the PUBLISHED one — what fal documents, what the catalog is keyed on, and what unmodel submits to.

alibaba/qwen-image-3/edit.note: Qwen Image 3 editing, conditional on a 1K/2K `resolution`.

argil/avatars/audio-to-video.note: Argil Avatars — the second preset-performer route, and the second witness that `image` is a per-model fact in this category.

blackforestlabs/flux-video-upscale.note: FLUX video upscaler — a vendor-namespaced id whose OpenAPI documents the internal route `/fal-ai/flux-video-upscale` (the ideogram/v4 precedent). The published model page for the vendor id renders no rate; the documented route's page does, and that is what pricing.json cites.

bria/fibo-edit/relight.note: Fibo Edit [Relight]. Provider-native only: its request is prompt-less by construction (`image_url`, `light_direction`, `light_type` are required), while the unified image-edit vocabulary requires a prompt and would therefore send a field this endpoint does not declare.

bytedance/seedance-2.0/text-to-video.note: Seedance 2.0 text-to-video — a 4k resolution tier its 2.5 sibling does not offer.

bytedance/seedance-2.5/image-to-video.note: Seedance 2.5 image-to-video. `image_url` opens the clip and `end_image_url` closes it — the first/last pair VideoImageRole exists for.

bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-vide.note: Seedance 2.5 reference-to-video: `image_urls`, `audio_urls` and `video_urls` are all reference LISTS the prompt addresses as @Image1/@Audio1/@Video1. The reference arm of VideoImageRole.

bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video.note: Seedance 2.5 text-to-video. `duration` is a string enum whose first member is "auto" — a length the model chooses — beside the seconds 4..30, which is why a duration list is filtered to the numeric members.

bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/edit.note: Seedream 5.0 Pro editing. Priced by output area PLUS an additive surcharge per extra input image.

bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/text-to-image.note: Seedream 5.0 Pro. Priced by output pixel AREA in two bands — a conditional whose tier the request settles only once a size is given.

cassetteai/sound-effects-generator.note: CassetteAI SFX. The one endpoint in this roster whose `duration` is REQUIRED (integer, 1–30) — which is why `unmodel/sfx` has a per-model required arm at all: everywhere else omitting the length is legal and means the provider's own default.

fal-ai/ace-step.note: ACE-Step. Its prompt is spelled `tags` (a comma-separated style list) and `lyrics` is separate and optional — so the curated textParam is `tags` and `lyrics` rides as an extra.

fal-ai/aura-sr.note: AuraSR. Its `upscale_factor` is a CONST 4: the endpoint upscales by four or not at all, which is the closed-`factors` arm of the row (`factor: 2` is a compile error naming 4).

fal-ai/bytedance/omnihuman/v1.5.note: OmniHuman 1.5 — a still, an audio track, and an optional `mask_url` limiting what moves.

fal-ai/bytedance/seed-speech/tts/v2.note: ByteDance Seed Speech v2: 41 voices whose names carry their languages, plus a flat mp3/opus codec field.

fal-ai/chatterbox/text-to-speech.note: Chatterbox. Its `audio_url` is a reference voice to clone rather than an input to transcribe, so it stays an extra: this category has no canonical word for "speak like this recording".

fal-ai/chatterbox/text-to-speech/multili.note: Chatterbox multilingual — `voice` is a language NAME here ("english", "japanese") rather than a speaker, which is why the row's voices and its languages are the same 23 words.

fal-ai/clarity-upscaler.note: Upscaler that steers on a prompt — the `factor?` + `prompt?` shape UpscaleParams is built around.

fal-ai/cohere-transcribe.note: Cohere's transcription model: a 14-member language enum of plain subtags, and a `max_new_tokens` ceiling that is an extra rather than a canonical word.

fal-ai/diffrhythm.note: DiffRhythm: lyrics to song. `lyrics` is the required input and `style_prompt` is the decoration, so the canonical `prompt` maps to the lyrics here — the one endpoint where the two words swap places. Its length is a two-member string enum ("95s" | "285s").

fal-ai/echomimic-v3.note: EchoMimic v3. The one avatar endpoint whose `prompt` is REQUIRED, which is why the category's prompt is a per-model extra rather than a canonical word — three of the eight rows have no prompt at all.

fal-ai/elevenlabs/music.note: ElevenLabs Music. Its length is `music_length_ms` — MILLISECONDS, which is exactly why the canonical word is `durationSeconds` and not `duration` — and its `output_format` is a COMPOSITE codec+rate enum (`mp3_44100_128`), so the row narrows only the codec half.

fal-ai/elevenlabs/sound-effects/v2.note: ElevenLabs Sound Effects v2, resold. A NARROWED reseller of the native `/v1/sound-generation`: `duration_seconds` caps at 22 rather than 30, `output_format` is a body field rather than a query param, `text` is capped at 450 characters, and there is no `model_id` because the route IS the model. That divergence is the point of curating it beside the native leaf.

fal-ai/elevenlabs/speech-to-text.note: ElevenLabs Scribe v1. The one route here with a `diarize` switch, which is what makes the canonical `diarization` expressible at fal at all.

fal-ai/elevenlabs/speech-to-text/scribe-.note: ElevenLabs Scribe v2 — adds `keyterms`, which is also what makes its price conditional (+30% when used).

fal-ai/elevenlabs/tts/eleven-v3.note: ElevenLabs v3. Its voice field is an OPEN string (the catalog is per-account and includes clones), so the row publishes no `voices` list and `voice` keeps the wide vocabulary.

fal-ai/elevenlabs/tts/multilingual-v2.note: ElevenLabs Multilingual v2 — the generation with `speed`, `style` and `similarity_boost`.

fal-ai/elevenlabs/tts/turbo-v2.5.note: ElevenLabs Turbo v2.5, at half the per-character rate of v3.

fal-ai/esrgan.note: Real-ESRGAN. Its factor is spelled `scale` rather than `upscale_factor` — the second spelling the row's `factorWire` exists for — and `model` names the checkpoint (R6 allow-list, reviewed 2026-08-25).

fal-ai/flux-2-max.note: FLUX.2 [max]. Tiered like flux-2-pro, at 2.3x the rate.

fal-ai/flux-2-pro.note: FLUX.2 [pro] — the anyOf[$ref ImageSize, string enum] `image_size` union, and a TIERED price (first megapixel apart from each extra) that never reaches ModelCost.

fal-ai/flux-2-pro/edit.note: FLUX.2 [pro] editing, tiered per megapixel across input AND output.

fal-ai/flux-2/edit.note: FLUX.2 [dev] editing — billed on input and output megapixels, with inputs resized to 1MP first.

fal-ai/flux-2/flash.note: The cheapest FLUX.2 arm at $0.005/MP — the low end of the per-megapixel band.

fal-ai/flux-general.note: FLUX.1 [dev] with the whole conditioning surface bolted on — LoRAs, ControlNets, ControlNet unions, IP-Adapters, EasyControl weights and a fill image, 32 parameters over six nested components. The widest input schema in the roster, and the reason `shared.gen.ts` earns its $ref dedup.

fal-ai/flux-lora.note: FLUX.1 [dev] with LoRA weights — carries a `loras` array of URL+scale objects.

fal-ai/flux-pro/kontext.note: FLUX.1 Kontext [pro] — single-image instruction editing. unmodel also serves Kontext first-party at `unmodel/black-forest-labs`.

fal-ai/flux-pro/kontext/max/multi.note: Kontext [max] multi — takes `image_urls` (a LIST) where its siblings take a single `image_url`. The multi-image arm the media naming rule has to classify as an array of image refs.

fal-ai/flux-pro/v1.1-ultra.note: FLUX1.1 [pro] ultra — sizes by `aspect_ratio` with no pixel field, so it is the aspectRatioEnum arm of this category rather than an imageSizeUnion one.

fal-ai/flux-pro/v1/fill.note: FLUX.1 [pro] fill — inpainting, so it carries a `mask_url` alongside `image_url`. The second media kind in this category.

fal-ai/flux/dev.note: The anyOf[$ref ImageSize, string enum] `image_size` union — the imageSizeUnion shape class.

fal-ai/flux/dev/image-to-image.note: FLUX.1 [dev] image-to-image — a `strength` re-render rather than an instruction edit.

fal-ai/flux/schnell.note: Same shape as flux/dev with a much tighter num_inference_steps ceiling (12 vs 50) — the per-endpoint range narrowing the IR exists for.

fal-ai/gemini-3.1-flash-tts.note: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS: thirty named voices and an 87-member language enum spelled as English NAMES ("English (US)"), which the generator maps back to primary subtags.

fal-ai/gemini-tts.note: Gemini TTS. `model` is a REAL wire field ("gemini-2.5-flash-tts" | "gemini-2.5-pro-tts") choosing the tier, and it also doubles the price — the sync-lipsync/v2 situation in the speech category. Allow-listed under R6, reviewed 2026-08-25.

fal-ai/gpt-image-1.5.note: GPT Image 1.5. Same size x quality conditional shape as gpt-image-2.

fal-ai/heygen/v3/lipsync/precision.note: HeyGen Avatar v3 lipsync, precision arm. The plan filed the two heygen v3 lipsync routes under `avatar`; their live schemas require `video_url` + `audio_url`, so by the input rule that splits this pair of categories they are lipsync. Spells the duration-mismatch idea `enable_dynamic_duration` — a third spelling beside sync-lipsync's `sync_mode` and latentsync's `loop_mode`, which is what keeps it out of the vocabulary.

fal-ai/heygen/v3/lipsync/speed.note: HeyGen Avatar v3 lipsync, speed arm — the same nine parameters as the precision route at half the rate.

fal-ai/hunyuan-3d/v3.1/pro/image-to-3d.note: Tencent's Hunyuan3D 3.1 Pro, image-driven. Its extra views are seven NAMED siblings (`back_image_url`, `top_image_url`, `left_front_image_url`, …) beside the required `input_image_url`, so the canonical `image` is the front view and the rest are extras.

fal-ai/hunyuan-3d/v3.1/pro/text-to-3d.note: The text-driven half of the same model. `generate_type` picks a textured mesh or a white one — the switch every vendor here spells differently, and the reason `texture` is not vocabulary.

fal-ai/hunyuan-3d/v3.1/rapid/image-to-3d.note: The fast tier: three parameters in all. Its response carries `material_mtl` and `texture` beside the mesh, which is the one place in this category where the OBJ sidecars are visible on the wire.

fal-ai/hunyuan-image/v3/text-to-image.note: Hunyuan Image 3.0, the plain text-to-image route. Its /instruct siblings are editing arms and are not curated in wave 1.

fal-ai/hunyuan3d/v2.note: Hunyuan3D 2.0, the octree-resolution generation. `textured_mesh` triples the price, which is the conditional rate its pricing row carries.

fal-ai/hunyuan3d/v2/turbo.note: The turbo arm of the same schema — identical parameter surface, so it shares a generated row. fal publishes NO rate for it: see data/fal/pricing.json.

fal-ai/hyper3d/rodin/v2.5.note: Hyper3D Rodin v2.5, and the only endpoint in this category that reads BOTH moods: `prompt` and `image_urls` are both optional and the prompt steers an image-driven generation. That is the both-arm of the row's `inputs`, and it is why `ThreeDModelNarrowing` has three populated arms rather than two. `image_urls` is a LIST — the `imageWireList` flag.

fal-ai/hyper3d/rodin/v2.5/text-to-3d.note: The text-only sibling of the route above: same dials, no image field at all. The pair is the clearest statement in the roster that `inputs` is a fact about a ROUTE rather than about a vendor.

fal-ai/ideogram/v3.note: Ideogram V3. `rendering_speed` selects one of three per-image rates.

fal-ai/inworld-tts.note: Inworld TTS: 118 named voices, each tagged with its language in the name ("Craig (en)").

fal-ai/kling-video/ai-avatar/v2/pro.note: Kling AI Avatar v2 Pro, at 2x the Standard rate.

fal-ai/kling-video/ai-avatar/v2/standard.note: Kling AI Avatar v2 Standard. Its `prompt` defaults to ".", which is fal's way of spelling "required by the wire, meaningless to the caller".

fal-ai/kling-video/lipsync/audio-to-vide.note: Kling LipSync. fal files it under text-to-video, which is exactly the lossiness that makes the verb map hand-curated. Its sibling /lipsync/text-to-video is excluded — that arm is TTS composed with lipsync.

fal-ai/kling-video/o1/video-to-video/edi.note: Kling O1 edit — curated on DEMAND, not on capability: it is the PREVIOUS generation of the Omni edit line (o1 published 2025-12-01, the curated o3/pro/video-to-video/edit 2026-02-04), and its schema is o3's minus `shot_type`. It brings one new $ref component of its own, `OmniVideoElementInput`, whose `frontal_image_url` is required where o3's KlingV3ImageElementInput makes it nullable. Ten newer o3 routes remain uncurated — see the o3-family sweep noted in `excluded.$comment`.

fal-ai/kling-video/o3/pro/video-to-video.note: Kling O3 Pro video-to-video edit — a source CLIP plus reference images, which is the one video row whose canonical input is `video` rather than `image`.

fal-ai/kling-video/v2.5-turbo/pro/image-.note: `duration` is a STRING enum here ("5" | "10") against veo3.1's ("4s" | "6s" | "8s") — same word, same type, different vocabulary. Also the only ui.field:"image" media hint in the wave-1a set (tail_image_url).

fal-ai/kling-video/v2.5-turbo/pro/text-t.note: The text-to-video sibling of the wave-1a kling v2.5-turbo row — same route shape, different endpoint id, which is exactly why fal needs no `videoFromImage` address.

fal-ai/kling-video/v2.6/pro/image-to-vid.note: Kling 2.6 Pro image-to-video, with a `voice_ids` array its text sibling has not got.

fal-ai/kling-video/v2.6/pro/text-to-vide.note: Kling 2.6 Pro. Two durations only ("5"|"10") where v3 offers thirteen.

fal-ai/kling-video/v3/pro/image-to-video.note: Kling 3.0 Pro image-to-video. Its first frame is `start_image_url`, not `image_url` — the media-naming rule has to read the stem rather than match a fixed name.

fal-ai/kling-video/v3/pro/motion-control.note: Kling v3 Pro motion control — a still driven by a reference clip's motion. The FIRST video row with a required, defaultless, non-media ENUM (`character_orientation`), which is why the routing probe reads the IR's enum rather than filling every required prop with the prompt. Its `image_url` is a CHARACTER reference, not an opening frame, but the media-naming rule files it as VideoImageRole's `first` and there is no `role` overlay kind to say otherwise; a caller writing role:"reference" is refused. Reachable through providerOptions.fal.character_orientation.

fal-ai/kling-video/v3/pro/text-to-video.note: Kling 3.0 Pro. `duration` is a STRING enum of the seconds 3..15 — the durationStringEnum class, and a different vocabulary from veo3.1's ("4s"|"6s"|"8s") for the same word.

fal-ai/kling-video/v3/standard/text-to-v.note: Kling 3.0 Standard, the cheaper arm of the same schema.

fal-ai/kokoro/american-english.note: Kokoro, one endpoint per language. Twenty American English voices — the largest of the nine lists, and the reason `voices` is per model rather than per adapter.

fal-ai/kokoro/brazilian-portuguese.note: Kokoro Brazilian Portuguese — three voices. fal serves NINE Kokoro languages, not the twelve the model's own card lists; the three the plan expected (German, Korean, Vietnamese) have no endpoint here.

fal-ai/kokoro/french.note: Kokoro French. Its `voice` is a CONST rather than an enum — one voice, `ff_siwis` — which is the single-value-enum lowering seen from the unified side.

fal-ai/latentsync.note: LatentSync. Carries `loop_mode` ("pingpong"|"loop") — a per-model extra, not vocabulary: sync-lipsync spells the same idea `sync_mode` with five arms, and one word two providers spell differently is not yet canonical.

fal-ai/lightx/relight.note: Light-X video relighting. Its canonical input is the CLIP (`video_url`, the only required field) and the prompt is OPTIONAL — omitted, Light-X auto-captions the video, which is exactly why VideoParamsBase types `prompt` as optional. `relight_parameters` is a nested `anyOf[$ref, null]` object, the fal-ai/flux-general `fill_image` lowering verbatim; FalPropSpec has no `props` for objects, so its own required `relight_prompt` is checked by fal rather than by unmodel. There is no relight VERB: bria, lightx, image-apps-v2 and iclight-v2 spell the same idea four ways and no two agree. `bria/fibo-edit/relight` is therefore curated only in the provider-native substrate (`unified: false`), not promoted into a guessed shared vocabulary. Two `note` overlays record what fal's prose gets wrong here.

fal-ai/longcat-single-avatar/image-audio.note: LongCat single-avatar, image + audio arm. Its /audio-to-video sibling is the still-less arm and is not curated — one route per shape is enough.

fal-ai/lyria2.note: Google's music model. fal files it under text-to-audio, which is exactly why the verb is curated here.

fal-ai/lyria3/pro.note: Lyria 3 Pro. Takes an optional `image_url` to condition on, and returns generated `lyrics` beside the audio.

fal-ai/minimax-music/v2.note: MiniMax Music 2. REQUIRES `lyrics_prompt` beside `prompt`; same honest refusal as music-3.

fal-ai/minimax-music/v2.6.note: MiniMax Music 2.6. Has a real `is_instrumental` switch — one of the two endpoints here where the canonical `instrumental` has anywhere to go.

fal-ai/minimax/hailuo-02/pro/image-to-vi.note: Hailuo 02 Pro. The one flat per-second rate in this category — no resolution field, no audio switch, so its estimate is a number rather than `undefined`.

fal-ai/minimax/hailuo-2.3/pro/text-to-vi.note: MiniMax Hailuo 2.3 [Pro] text-to-video — two parameters and nothing else (`prompt`, `prompt_optimizer`): no duration, no resolution, no aspect ratio, so through the unified surface it takes a prompt and reports every other canonical field as unsupported. Curated for its PRICE shape as much as its output: $0.49 per generation is the only flat per-generation rate in the video roster, which makes it the one fal video endpoint whose `estimate.costUSD` is an exact number from a request body alone. It is NOT the current MiniMax generation — `minimax/h3/{text,image}-to-video` (Hailuo 3, 2026-07-31) are curated above and are a generation newer than 2.3 (2025-10-27).

fal-ai/minimax/speech-02-hd.note: Nested $ref inputs (VoiceSetting / AudioSetting / PronunciationDict) — the component-lowering case. Its `output_format` is `url | hex`, a DELIVERY switch rather than a codec, which is why the row publishes no codecs.

fal-ai/minimax/speech-2.8-hd.note: MiniMax Speech 2.8 HD. Its text param is `prompt` where the 02 generation spells it `text`, and its voice lives NESTED in `voice_setting.voice_id` — so this row publishes no `voiceWire` and the canonical `voice` is refused by name, pointing at providerOptions.

fal-ai/minimax/speech-2.8-turbo.note: MiniMax Speech 2.8 Turbo — same surface as the HD arm at a lower rate.

fal-ai/nano-banana.note: The original Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image), flat per-image.

fal-ai/nano-banana-2.note: Google's Gemini 3 Pro Image. `resolution` multiplies the rate and two booleans add surcharges — the conditional-pricing case that keeps rates out of ModelCost.

fal-ai/nano-banana-2/edit.note: aspectRatioEnum + resolutionEnum, and a multi-image `image_urls` array.

fal-ai/nano-banana-pro.note: Nano Banana Pro. Same conditional shape as nano-banana-2 with a narrower `resolution` enum (no 0.5K).

fal-ai/nano-banana-pro/edit.note: The edit arm of nano-banana-pro, conditional on `resolution`.

fal-ai/nano-banana/edit.note: The edit arm of the original Nano Banana, flat per-image.

fal-ai/pixverse/lipsync.note: PixVerse lipsync. The one endpoint here whose `audio_url` is OPTIONAL: it also takes `text` + `voice_id` and speaks the line itself. unmodel's canonical `audio` is required, so the TTS arm is reachable only through `providerOptions` — deliberately, per the excluded kling text-to-video row.

fal-ai/pixverse/v6/text-to-video.note: PixVerse v6. `duration` is a free integer 1..15 rather than an enum, so `duration` keeps the wide `number`.

fal-ai/qwen-3-tts/text-to-speech/1.7b.note: Qwen 3 TTS (1.7B). Declares BOTH `text` and `prompt`: `text` is what is spoken and `prompt` is a style instruction, so the curated textParam is `text` and `prompt` stays a per-model extra.

fal-ai/recraft/upscale/crisp.note: Recraft crisp upscale. Takes NO factor at all — the empty-`factors` arm, which types `factor` as `never` at the call site instead of letting a caller ask for a multiplier the route has nowhere to put.

fal-ai/recraft/v3/text-to-image.note: Recraft V3. A vector `style` doubles the rate, so the tier key is a style name rather than a size or a speed.

fal-ai/seedvr/upscale/image.note: SeedVR2 for stills. Offers both a `factor` mode and a `target` one through `upscale_mode`; unmodel's canonical `factor` drives the first and the second is reachable as an extra.

fal-ai/seedvr/upscale/video.note: SeedVR2 for clips — the sibling that makes `sources` a real narrowing rather than a constant: same vendor, same product, `video_url` instead of `image_url`.

fal-ai/speech-to-text/turbo.note: The turbo arm of the same route, same surface and same rate.

fal-ai/stable-audio-25/text-to-audio.note: Stable Audio 2.5. Its length is `seconds_total` — a third spelling for the same idea, and the reason the row states the wire name rather than assuming one.

fal-ai/stable-audio-3/medium/text-to-aud.note: Stable Audio 3 Medium — the one music endpoint here with a flat codec enum, so the only one whose canonical `outputFormat` narrows to a list.

fal-ai/stable-audio-3/small/sfx/base/tex.note: Stable Audio 3 Small SFX, base arm — the same surface as its sibling with different sampler defaults (50 steps, guidance 7). fal-ai/stable-audio-3/small/sfx/text-to-.note: Stable Audio 3 Small SFX. Stability is the fifth SFX vendor and the one unmodel already serves natively elsewhere; it publishes the widest length range here (1–120s, default 30) and the only SEPARATE `bitrate` field, a kbps-suffixed string ("192k").

fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v2.note: `model` is a REAL wire field ("lipsync-2" | "lipsync-2-pro") and stays on the wire; the route is still selected by the `endpoint` pseudo-param. fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v2/pro.note: sync. lipsync-2-pro as its own endpoint. Same three parameters as v2 minus the `model` field, because the id already says which model.

fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v3.note: Clip-in lipsync. Carries a nested `options` object two components deep (Sync3GenerationOptions → Sync3ActiveSpeakerDetection).

fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v3/image-to-video.note: The still-driven twin of sync-lipsync/v3 — image in, video out. The split that makes lipsync and avatar separate packs rather than one `sources` arm.

fal-ai/trellis.note: Microsoft TRELLIS — structured-latent 3D generation from one image, and the cheapest row in the category at $0.02.

fal-ai/trellis-2.note: TRELLIS 2, with thirty parameters — the widest per-endpoint extras surface in this category, all of them sampler and UV-unwrap dials that no second vendor spells the same way.

fal-ai/triposr.note: Stability's TripoSR. Sub-second feed-forward reconstruction; its `output_format` is a two-value glb/obj enum, one of the four spellings that kept `format` out of the vocabulary.

fal-ai/veo3.1.note: fal-ai/veo3 was already GONE when this plan was written — veo3.1 is the live id. Its price is conditional on `generate_audio`, which is why conditional rates never reach ModelCost.

fal-ai/veo3.1/extend-video.note: Veo 3.1 extend. Its `duration` and `resolution` are `const` rather than enums — fal's single-value spelling, which lowers to a one-member enum and therefore still classifies.

fal-ai/veo3.1/fast.note: Veo 3.1 Fast — half the rate of the base row, same conditional shape (generate_audio x resolution).

fal-ai/veo3.1/first-last-frame-to-video.note: Veo 3.1 first-and-last-frame interpolation: `first_frame_url` AND `last_frame_url`, both required. The endpoint that makes VideoImageRole's "last" arm load-bearing.

fal-ai/veo3.1/reference-to-video.note: Veo 3.1 reference-to-video — the last member of the veo3.1 base family. `duration` is a `const "8s"`, the one-value-enum spelling extend-video already documents, and this is the FIRST video row whose required set includes a media ARRAY (`image_urls`), which is why the two probe derivations had to learn the `reference` role and the array wrap. fal-ai/wan/v2.2-a14b/text-to-video.note: Wan 2.2 A14B. Lengths are `num_frames` at a chosen `frames_per_second` rather than a `duration` field, so this row publishes no duration vocabulary at all.

fal-ai/wan/v2.7/image-to-video.note: Wan 2.7 image-to-video, which also accepts a `video_url` to continue from and an `audio_url` to drive lip motion — three media kinds on one route, none of them required.

fal-ai/wan/v2.7/text-to-video.note: Wan 2.7. `duration` is an INTEGER enum (2..15) where kling's is a string enum of the same numbers — the durationNumber class beside durationStringEnum.

fal-ai/wizper.note: fal-ai/whisper is gone; wizper is the live Whisper-v3 endpoint. Billed per compute-second, so it carries an `unpriced` reason rather than a rate. Two `const` properties (chunk_level, version) — the single-value-enum lowering.

fal-ai/z-image/turbo.note: Z-Image Turbo — the cheapest row in the category at $0.005/MP, and the one per-megapixel page that states no rounding rule.

hitem3d/hi3d/v3.0/image-to-3d.note: Hi3D v3.0. `model` is a REAL wire field — a `const "hi3dv3.0"` naming the checkpoint — and stays on the wire while the route is still selected by the `endpoint` pseudo-param. Allow-listed under R6, reviewed 2026-08-25 against the live schema.

krea/v2/large/text-to-image.note: Krea 2 large. unmodel also serves Krea first-party (`unmodel/krea`); this is the same model behind fal's queue.

lightricks/ltx-2.5/text-to-video/pro.note: LTX-2.5 Pro. Its `duration` enum is [6, 8, 10, "auto"] with NO declared type — a mixed-type enum that lowers by its first member, which is why the numeric filter on the duration list is not cosmetic.

openai/gpt-image-2.note: ChatGPT Images 2.0. Priced per size x quality PLUS unbounded token charges, so its estimate is undefined however the request is written.

excluded.$comment: Whole fal categories and specific ids unmodel deliberately does not serve. A reason here is what keeps a future roster widening from quietly re-adding them — and, since v0.3.x, what a CALLER gets: `scripts/codegen-fal.ts` emits this block as `FAL_EXCLUDED` / `FAL_EXCLUDED_CATEGORIES` in src/providers/fal/gen/endpoints.gen.ts, and `runFalChecks` hands the reason back as a warning when a request names an excluded id, instead of leaving it at a bare `unknown_model` that reads as catalog lag. Only `endpoints` is enforced; see `categories`.

categories.$comment: PROSE ONLY — nothing enforces these keys, and two of them never could: `ffmpeg-api` and `workflow-utils` are not fal `category` values (those routes report `video-to-video`, a category unmodel serves), so the audit read them as nothing at all and re-proposed the endpoints every week. Enforcement lives in `excluded.endpoints`, which `bun run codegen:fal:audit` subtracts from the uncurated list; the concrete ffmpeg / workflow-utilities ids are recorded there as of 2026-08-26. These entries stay because the ARGUMENT for skipping a whole family is worth keeping, and it is shipped as `FAL_EXCLUDED_CATEGORIES` for the same reason.
categories.3d-to-3d: 12 endpoints that take a MESH and return one — retopology, segmentation, retexture, rigging, part splitting. Real operations with no unmodel verb: `unmodel/3d` asks for an object to be MADE, and a route that refines one you already have is a different question. A `mesh` category is the honest home for them if they are ever wanted.
categories.ffmpeg-api: Plumbing (concat, trim, mux). No model, nothing to validate beyond a file list — the full argument, and the eleven live ids it covers, are in `excluded.endpoints` under `fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/compose`.
categories.llm: openrouter passthrough — unmodel ships the real openrouter provider, with its own catalog and availability data.
categories.subtitles: Plumbing — a rendering step over an stt result.
categories.training: 57 endpoints that start a fine-tune, not a validated inference request.
categories.vision: 34 endpoints doing image-in/text-out — `unmodel/chat` already owns that shape with real multimodal message types.
categories.workflow-utils: Plumbing — the same argument as `ffmpeg-api`, and the same place to look: `excluded.endpoints`, `fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/compose`. Note the live ids are `fal-ai/workflow-utilities/*`, not `workflow-utils/*`.

Serving it means teaching the generator a documented fallback order, which is new generator work rather than a cheap row. Its price is the unpopulated $0-per-compute-second template besides.
endpoints.fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/compose: fal's media plumbing — compose, trim, scale, mux, blend, extract a frame. `excluded.categories` has said "Plumbing." since wave 1 and it never fired: these report `x-fal-metadata.category: "video-to-video"` (probed live 2026-08-26), which IS a category unmodel serves, so `codegen:fal:audit` re-proposed them on every run — the keys `ffmpeg-api` and `workflow-utils` are not fal category values and never were. The sharper reason, in the voice of the `3d-to-3d` entry above: unmodel validates a MODEL request, and these have no model — no model id beyond the endpoint id, nothing to put in a catalog row, and a $0.001-per-compute-second rate that this repo's pricing law sends to "no cost + a caveat" (the wizper precedent), so the row would be an empty catalog entry. There is no verb either: `fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/compose` takes `{tracks: Track[]}` and nothing else, which is a file list rather than a request. Two of them do carry real bounds (`trim-video`'s `start_time`/`duration`, and prose-only rules like waveform's odd-numbered `smoothing_window`), so "nothing to validate" is overstated — but a validated file list is still not a model call. This list is the complete live set: one clean `bun run codegen:fal:audit` crawl of all 1,472 endpoints on 2026-08-26 found these eleven ffmpeg/workflow-utilities ids active and uncurated in served categories.

endpoints.fal-ai/imageutils/rembg: Background removal — the family wave 1 excluded without recording why, which is exactly the state that produces "why isn't X curated?". Every one of these routes is PROMPT-LESS (probed live 2026-08-26: fal-ai/imageutils/rembg, fal-ai/birefnet/v2, fal-ai/ben/v2/image, fal-ai/bria/background/remove, fal-ai/ideogram/remove-background, pixelcut/background-removal and veed/video-background-removal each declare `image_url` or `video_url` and no prompt), and `unmodel/image-edit` requires a prompt (vocabulary/image-edit.ts:126) which the fal adapter writes unconditionally (unified-image-edit.ts:445) — so promoting one into that adapter would send a field the endpoint does not declare on every call. `bria/fibo-edit/relight` is the substrate-only precedent: curated for exact direct requests with `unified: false`, and deliberately absent from the prompt-required adapter. The imageEdit `operation` arm that would carve out a prompt-less shape was offered and declined twice. A cut-out is also not what an EDIT means in this vocabulary: the output is the same picture with the subject isolated, which is a different artifact rather than a differently-instructed one. Wire-only today: `fal.imageEdit({ endpoint, image_url })`.
endpoints.fal-ai/kling-video/lipsync/text-to-video: Text + voice arm — that is TTS composed with lipsync, and composing it here would hide which half failed.
endpoints.fal-ai/lightx/recamera: Light-X's camera sibling of the curated `fal-ai/lightx/relight`, decided in the same wave rather than left unrecorded. It takes `video_url` plus `camera`, `mode`, `trajectory` and `target_pose` (probed live 2026-08-26) and re-shoots a clip along a virtual camera path. `unmodel/video` has no vocabulary for camera motion — no canonical word describes a trajectory, and the nested objects that carry one would be checked only for being records — so the row would be a name with per-model extras and nothing canonical to narrow, which is a catalog entry pretending to be a validator. It is also the clearest evidence that "relight" is the wrong axis for a verb: one vendor, two routes, asked for the same way and differing only in what they change. Wire-only today: `fal.video({ endpoint: "fal-ai/lightx/recamera", video_url, … })`.
endpoints.fal-ai/smart-turn: Turn detection, not transcription — no unmodel verb fits it.
endpoints.fal-ai/speech-to-text/stream: Streaming variants are a socket surface, not a queue submit — out of scope for a request validator.
endpoints.fal-ai/topaz/upscale/image: The pre-split Topaz image route. Still serves — the Platform API returns a real document and the playground renders — but fal has DELISTED it: `?endpoint_id=` answers with no `metadata` block and the roster crawl does not contain it. Its `model` enum (11) is a strict SUBSET of the precision+generative pair curated above (15): it lacks High Fidelity V3, Wonder 3.5, Wonder 2 and Recover 3, and its 19 properties are exactly that pair's union. Curating a delisted id would also make `codegen:fal:audit` report it GONE forever, since that check diffs against the listing. Verified live 2026-08-26.
endpoints.fal-ai/topaz/upscale/video: The pre-split Topaz video route, delisted like its image sibling (no listing `metadata`, absent from the roster crawl). Its properties are IDENTICAL to topaz/upscale/video/precision; only the `model` enum differs — it carries Starlight and Nyx, which the precision route does not. Starlight is not lost by excluding it: topaz/upscale/video/generative serves a NEWER Starlight (Precise 2.6 vs 2.5), is listed and active, and is curated above. The blocker is price: this route's page quotes one flat table with no model dimension ($0.01/s up to 720p, $0.02/s to 1080p, $0.08/s above) while serving Starlight, which the generative route prices at $1.20 per 10s at 1080p. Two published sentences that cannot both be true is not a catalog row. Verified live 2026-08-26.

endpoints.topaz/upscale/image/creative: Topaz's Bloom family at fal (`model`: Bloom 2 | Bloom | Bloom Realism, plus `autoprompt` and `creativity`), listed and active — held back for one missing fact, and the fact is the price. Nobody has transcribed https://fal.ai/models/topaz/upscale/image/creative, and a curated endpoint with neither a rate nor an `unpriced` reason FAILS codegen; a rate guessed from its precision sibling would be a number a caller treats as a budget. Worth naming as the strongest candidate for the next widening: unmodel's NATIVE topaz provider already catalogs Bloom 2 and Bloom Realism with hand-transcribed settings (src/providers/topaz/models.ts), so fal's resale of the same product is the one Topaz family visible on one half of the package and not the other. Verified live 2026-08-26.
endpoints.topaz/upscale/image/transparent: An alpha-preserving variant of the precision route with NO `model` field at all — three properties (`image_url`, `output_format`, `upscale_factor`), so as a catalog row it would be its precision sibling minus the network choice. Held back on the same missing price transcription as the two `creative` routes, and recorded rather than left to the audit to re-propose every week. Verified live 2026-08-26.
endpoints.topaz/upscale/video/creative: The clip half of the same Bloom/creative family (`prompt`, `creativity`, `realism`, `sharp`), listed and active, held back for the same reason as topaz/upscale/image/creative: its price sentence has not been transcribed, and pricing.json may not be silent about a curated row. Verified live 2026-08-26.
endpoints.tripo3d/h3.1/multiview-to-3d: Requires `image_urls` with minItems 2, and `unmodel/3d`'s `image` is ONE reference. A route that cannot be called with a single view cannot be half-served through this vocabulary; its v2.5 sibling is curated in because there the extra angles are optional.
endpoints.tripo3d/triposplat: Gaussian splats rather than a mesh. The output is a point cloud with per-point spherical harmonics — a different artifact with different tooling, and `Modality`'s new `"3d"` member would be claiming more than it means.
